uncited: Parametric Path Generation constructs camera trajectories by evaluating explicit mathematical functions of a scalar parameter (typically angle or time) to produce a sequence of camera poses [S1, S3, S4].

It solves the problem of generating smooth, continuous novel views from a sparse set of training images by defining the geometry of the path analytically rather than interpolating between discrete keyframes.

It differs from [Sparse Trajectory Generation](7215-sparse-trajectory-generation.md) by relying on closed-form equations for position and orientation, and from [Synthetic Camera Trajectory Generation](7942-synthetic-camera-trajectory-generation.md) by deriving parameters directly from scene statistics (e.g., camera bounding boxes) rather than arbitrary artistic constraints.
The family shares the mechanism of mapping a scalar parameter $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ (or a linear time interval) to a 4x4 transformation matrix $\mathbf{P}$.
**Scene Analysis**: Compute scene statistics (centroid, bounding box, or percentiles) from input training poses to define the spatial bounds of the trajectory [S1, S2, S3, S4].
**Parameterization**: Define position $\mathbf{c}(\theta)$ and orientation (look-at direction $\mathbf{z}(\theta)$, up vector $\mathbf{u}(\theta)$) as functions of $\theta$.
**Pose Construction**: Assemble the rotation matrix $\mathbf{R}$ from orthogonal basis vectors and translation $\mathbf{t}$ into $\mathbf{P} = [\mathbf{R} | \mathbf{t}]$ [S1, S3, S4].
**Sampling**: Evaluate the functions at $N$ evenly spaced intervals, excluding the final duplicate point to ensure a closed loop without redundancy [S1, S2, S3, S4].
Parametric path generation is a foundational technique in NeRF (Neural Radiance Fields) and volume rendering novel view synthesis.
The spiral path generation method was popularized by the original NeRF implementation [S1, S3, S4], which used it to generate training views for forward-facing scenes.

The elliptical and orbit variants emerged as adaptations to handle different scene geometries and rendering pipelines, often found in open-source NeRF implementations and visualization tools [S2, S1].
